The adenine nucleotides in mitochondria and cytosol are not in equilibrium, but the adenine nucleotide phosphorylation potential is similar in the two subcellular compartments.

the subcellular concentrations of ATP and ADP, and the phosphorylation potentials, and the regulation of the adenine nucleotide systems in the perfused rat liver.
the adenine nucleotide concentrations and the adenylate energy charge of subcellular compartments in the living cell.
the adenine nucleotides in the subcellular compartments of the living cell and the role these nucleotides play as modulators of metabolic processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, under the conditions studied here, the adenine nucleotide phosphorylation potentials of both mitochondrial and cytosol are not constant, but are dependent on the metabolic state.
the ATP and ADP concentrations in the cytosolic and mitochondrial fractions of perfused rat livers are not constant and depend upon the metabolic state of the organ.

the mitochondrial and cytosol ATP systems of the perfused liver are interrelated and dependent upon each other, but that the degree of interdependence is dependent upon the metabolic state of the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adenine nucleotide concentrations and phosphorylation potentials in the cytosolic and mitochondrial compartments are not constant, but are dynamic, depending upon the metabolic state of the liver.
the adenine nucleotide concentrations are not only a function of the metabolic state but also of the subcellulation of the adenine nucleotides.
the ATP/ADPi ratios in the mitochondria are higher than that in the cytosolic compartment and that the mitochondrial and cytosol systems are linked through the ATP/ADPI ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial ATP/ADP ratio is much more tightly regulated than the cytosolic ATP/ADP.
the ATP and ADP levels in the cytosolic compartment of the cell are tightly coupled to the mitochondrial ATP and ADP pools.
the ATP/ADPtot ratios of both the mitochondrial and cytosol are highly dependent on the metabolic state and are not constant as has been previously thought.
